features.description: Interpret the Son of Man title and subsequent natural masculine personal reference.
Interpret the bounded abstract on his mægenðrymme, in his majesty.
Recover the understood coming predicate in the coordinated angels clause without turning nominative angels into a mid object.
Interpret the exact sentence-initial then adverb, not a temporal subordinate clause or comparative than.
Recognize the source genitive characterizing the throne, with Cook153.f explicitly supplied.
Interpret the exact future passive with postposed nominative plural subject, supplied participle and before phrase.
Interpret the exact separates-them-into-two-groups frame; source verb and division expression supplied.
Interpret the supplied swā-swā comparison; existing separating object/fram-case relations remain visible.
Interpret the exact placement clause and elliptical final hand; accusative follows this bounded side-expression and bare noun rather than a universal direction rule or syncretic adjective ending.

regular_dependencies.description: Produce the selected article forms agreeing with their own noun in gender, number and nominative/genitive/dative/accusative case.
Produce limiting relational genitives. Follow Cook's exercise target: dependent first, head noun without its own article; retain the dependent's required article.
Use taught locative on with dative ('in/on'); this is a selected construction, not a universal spatial rule.
Use fram plus dative for the entity from which something is separated, in an explicitly supplied separating frame.
Adjectives agree with their own noun/referent in case, number and gender; attributive and ordinary positive predicate uses are taught.

Ordinary attributive adjectives are weak after article/demonstrative; bare ordinary adjectives are strong. After possessives Cook permits strong and sometimes weak; no universal possessive→weak rule and no new rule for adjectives after limiting genitives.
Comparatives are weak attributively and predicatively; full paradigms include transparently derived genitive plural contractions and licensed -ena selections.
his/hiere/hiera are invariant possessors; possessor reference determines choice, while the head keeps its own case/number.
Promote eall strong NGDA and introduce image-checked longǣlc strong NGDA. Complete models do not teach unrelated indefinite pronouns, partitives, adverbial quantifier idioms or weak paradigms.

For assigned accusative-object verbs, present or preterite wesan/bēon or weorðan + past participle expresses passive. Finite auxiliary agrees with the nominative subject. Agent omitted in productive tasks; no new fram-agent rule needed. Wesan often presents state/result and weorðan event, but not an absolute contrast or one-to-one English tense mapping.
Mid + dative names an accompanying person or cargo.
Present indicative can refer to future events where context supplies futurity; English will/shall need not produce willan.
Tō+dative gives a destination with come/go/fly.

note: All regular dependency IDs were reconciled against the actual prior grammar register and released Unit10 grammar proposal. No source-only clause is independently tested without its help.
